title: Novara Systems Hosting & Security Discovery
header:
Date: 2027-06-21
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Owen Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Novara CISO), Marcus Reed (Platform), Ibrahim Kaur (DevOps), Sophie Lin (Product)
Recording: yes (auto)
summary: Discovery focused on security posture and hosting tradeoffs (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private). Primary concerns: SOC 2 evidence, KMS/HSM integration, SSO/SAML and RBAC alignment, audit logs and retention, data residency. Novara leaning toward dedicated or private due to regulated data and latency needs; wants performance baseline and SOC2 artifacts. Agreed next steps: send SOC2/ISO docs, topology diagram, and schedule a private deployment feasibility session with infra team.
topics: SOC 2 / ISO compliance status and artifacts
SSO / SAML flow and SCIM provisioning
Audit logs, retention, and export (SIEM integration)
Encryption: customer-managed KMS vs Redwood-managed keys
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs (latency, cost, data residency)
Network topology: VPC peering, private link, egress controls
action_items: Maya: Share SOC 2 Type II report and ISO snapshot + compliance matrix by 2027-06-23
Owen: Export sample audit log schema and retention options, include SIEM webhook format by 2027-06-24
Marcus: Provide tentative traffic profile and tail latency requirements (p95/p99) by 2027-06-25
Ibrahim: Confirm which cloud region and whether they need on-prem connector by 2027-06-24
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC2/ISO artifacts and network diagram
Schedule infra deep-dive (private deployment feasibility) with Novara infra team next week
Redwood to provision a short benchmark (p95/p99) for Nova's sample workload if Novara shares sample requests
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on this account. We got Owen, our solutions engineer, on the line too. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Lena Ortiz: Good, thanks. Running a bit behind with a ticket but we're here.
[00:12] Marcus Reed: Hey — Marcus here.
[00:14] Owen Patel: Hi all. Quick agenda: compliance posture, hosting options, keys/audit logs, then we can jump into Qs.
[00:25] Sophie Lin: That works. We're mainly trying to understand whether we can use hosted or if we need dedicated/private because of our regulated workflows.
[00:33] Maya Chen: Totally. Maybe start with a quick sketch of Novara's constraints? Lena, can you run through the security and compliance guardrails?
[00:41] Lena Ortiz: Sure. We're a payments-adjacent platform — not a PSP but we touch cardholder adjacent PII. We need SOC 2 Type II for vendor management, ISO 27001 is a nice-to-have, and our legal wants KMS customer-managed keys for production data. Also SSO with SAML and SCIM for provisioning.
[01:02] Marcus Reed: And low-latency inference for real-time fraud scoring — we're worried about p99 latency under 10ms for the hot path, otherwise it affects checkout flow.
[01:11] Owen Patel: 10ms p99 is tight for general-purpose LLMs; curious whether that's per-token or end-to-end inference.
[01:17] Marcus Reed: End-to-end scoring call, single-turn, ~512 tokens worst case but typically much smaller.
[01:25] Ibrahim Kaur: Ops note: we want full audit logs forwarded to our SIEM (Splunk) and retention for 3 years; also role-based access so only small set of service accounts can call production models.
[01:38] Maya Chen: Great, that's specific. A couple clarifications: Redwood Hosted can be configured with customer-managed keys via our KMS integration for private deployments; hosted has Redwood-managed encryption keys by default but we offer a Dedicated and Private path for CMK and VPC isolation.
[01:56] Lena Ortiz: When you say KMS integration, are you referring to our cloud KMS or Redwood's HSM? We need HSM-backed keys per policy.
[02:05] Owen Patel: We integrate with cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and also have an HSM-backed option for Private deployments where customers can bring an HSM or integrate via Cloud HSM. The transcript above may mis-say HSM as "H M S" in our notes :).
[02:22] Sophie Lin: Important for us — we also have strict data residency requirements; EU data must stay in eu-west. Can Redwood pin model serving by region?
[02:31] Maya Chen: Yes — we have routing policies and region pinning. For Hosted, you can select region endpoints; Dedicated gives you committed pools in a region; Private gives you full on-prem or VPC control.
[02:42] Marcus Reed: Can you walk through audit logs? What kind of events do you capture?
[02:47] Owen Patel: We capture request metadata, token counts, model version, request payload hash, API key id, and we can emit structured logs to S3/GCS or stream to your SIEM via webhooks. Retention policies are configurable per-account in Dedicated and Private; hosted accounts have default retention but enterprise plans can extend.
[03:03] Ibrahim Kaur: Are logs PII-scrubbed automatically? We can't forward raw inputs that might contain sensitive cardholder data.
[03:11] Owen Patel: Good callout — we offer redaction hooks and tokenization policies — redaction is done client-side at your option or we can do a redaction pass before logs are shipped if you want Redwood to help. For PCI-level data we'd recommend not sending full raw sensitive fields to Hosted.
[03:27] Lena Ortiz: For SOC2, we need the Type II. Do you have it?
[03:32] Maya Chen: Yes we have SOC 2 Type II, and we also maintain ISO 27001 attestation. I'll share the cert and a compliance matrix after the call.
[03:40] Sophie Lin: Can you include the control mappings for KMS and RBAC? Our procurement wants to see who owns the key rotation responsibilities.
[03:47] Maya Chen: Absolutely. We'll send a matrix mapping Redwood controls to common frameworks — plus details on key rotation, separation of duties, and audit trail.
[03:55] Marcus Reed: About RBAC — we want granular token-level permissions, e.g., sandbox access vs prod access, per-team model permissions. How is that modeled?
[04:04] Owen Patel: We support API-key scoping and fine-grained RBAC in Dedicated/Private with token-level granularity. For Hosted we have scoped API keys and role assignments. For enterprises we can synchronize your IdP groups via SCIM so roles map automatically.
[04:18] Ibrahim Kaur: SSO: we use SAML 2.0 and Okta. Do you support Just-In-Time provisioning?
[04:24] Maya Chen: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning; JIT often depends on your IdP settings but we can accommodate Okta flows — we have sample metadata and a tutorial.
[04:34] Lena Ortiz: If we go Dedicated, what's on our network? Do you need cross-connect or VPC peering?
[04:40] Owen Patel: For Dedicated we can do VPC peering or PrivateLink depending on cloud. You get a dedicated pool in a customer VPC with private endpoints. Private (on-prem) is a different bundle — we ship a customer-managed control plane and you run inference nodes behind your network.
[04:55] Marcus Reed: Performance: we may favor on-prem inference for p99 latency, but that's higher ops cost. Would Redwood run benchmarks against our sample requests?
[05:03] Maya Chen: Yes — if you can share sample payloads (anonymized) we can run a short benchmark on Dedicated config and share p95/p99 numbers, kernel-level profiles and cost estimate.
[05:13] Sophie Lin: Cost aside, what are the fallback policies? If Dedicated cluster saturated do you fail open to Hosted?
[05:20] Owen Patel: We have routing policies — you can define failover to a lower-cost or hosted variant, or fail closed. For regulated data you might prefer degrade or queue.
[05:30] Ibrahim Kaur: About retention, 3 years retention for logs — is that possible?
[05:34] Owen Patel: Yes in Dedicated/Private you can set arbitrary retention, we'll quote the storage cost. Hosted has standard retention tiers but enterprise can request custom.
[05:43] Lena Ortiz: Can you expose KMS audit events to our SIEM? We need key usage logs.
[05:49] Owen Patel: We can export key usage via CloudTrail (if using AWS KMS) and surface a copy in our audit stream. For HSM it's similar but depends on how the HSM publishes usage events. We'll document the integration steps.
[06:02] Marcus Reed: Any concerns around model KV cache or memory leaking PII? We do few-shot prompts with internal context.
[06:09] Owen Patel: We allow KV cache partitioning and TTL for cached contexts; we also provide policies to avoid persistent caching of sensitive prompts. For private deployments you can disable KV persistence entirely.
[06:22] Sophie Lin: Is there a standard data flow diagram you can share — endpoints, what goes to Redwood, what stays in our VPC?
[06:29] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll attach a network topology diagram and an example data flow map.
[06:34] Lena Ortiz: On the legal side, we need data processing addendum (DPA) and SOC 2. Also want to discuss breach notification timelines.
[06:42] Maya Chen: We have a standard DPA and can negotiate SLAs and breach notification windows for enterprise contracts.
[06:49] Ibrahim Kaur: For the CMK, does Redwood do envelope encryption or do we hold the master key?
[06:54] Owen Patel: We support envelope encryption. You hold the master key in your KMS/HSM and Redwood holds derived data keys for ephemeral use — we never store the master key. For Private deployments you can keep all keys in your HSM and Redwood will never see plaintext keys.
[07:07] Marcus Reed: Great. Any regulatory red flags we should watch?
[07:11] Maya Chen: Only that Hosted may not satisfy some on-premise-only controls for certain regulators; Dedicated or Private usually required for strict data residency and HSM-only key policies.
[07:20] Sophie Lin: Can we get a short security runbook for our GRC team?
[07:23] Maya Chen: We'll send a security runbook — includes onboarding checklist, network config, auditing, and escalation points.
[07:29] Lena Ortiz: About encryption in transit — TLS mutual auth?
[07:33] Owen Patel: TLS 1.2+; mutual TLS is available for Private and can be configured for Dedicated. Hosted endpoints support TLS with client certs available on request.
[07:44] Marcus Reed: Let's talk timeline — procurement wants a vendor decision in 6 weeks. If we need a pilot how long to stand up Dedicated?
[07:51] Maya Chen: For a pilot we can provision a small Dedicated pool in 2–3 weeks once legal and network controls are signed off. Private on-premers usually take longer depending on your infra team.
[08:03] Ibrahim Kaur: Any automated cert rotation or key compromise playbooks?
[08:07] Owen Patel: Yes, rotation is automated for Redwood-managed keys; with CMK you control rotation via KMS. We can share our compromise and rotation playbook.
[08:15] Sophie Lin: Are there known integrations for Okta SCIM we can reference?
[08:19] Maya Chen: We'll share the Okta SCIM app config and SAML metadata.
[08:24] [09:00] (brief hold music)
[09:04] Marcus Reed: Quick follow-up — can Redwood support IP allow-listing at the account level?
[09:09] Owen Patel: Yes, IP allow-listing and VPC-only endpoints are supported on Dedicated/Private. Hosted has static egress ranges we can provide.
[09:18] Lena Ortiz: If we go with Hosted with CMK, are there any shared responsibilities we need to call out?
[09:24] Maya Chen: Responsibilities: you manage the master key lifecycle and access policies in your KMS; Redwood manages the runtime and derived keys. We'll provide a shared responsibility matrix.
[09:34] Sophie Lin: Ok, sounds like we need the SOC2 docs, network diagram, sample payloads for performance test, and the SCIM/SAML config.
[09:43] Maya Chen: Yes, our action items are noted. We'll send an initial packet within two business days.
[09:48] Lena Ortiz: Awesome. Any blockers on our side right now?
[09:51] Marcus Reed: We'll need internal approval to share samples but should be able to anonymize.
[09:55] Maya Chen: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the doc pack and schedule the infra deep-dive.
[09:59] (call ends)
